high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Intervenes in Rising Deposit Interest Rates
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has issued urgent directives to regional branches regarding commercial banks' rising deposit rates. Recent surveys by MB Securities reveal that actual deposit rates at bank counters and through negotiated deposit contracts remain significantly higher than officially published rates. The SBV ordered regional branches to directly inspect interest rate implementation at commercial banks and immediately report any violations to banking supervision authorities. This intervention signals the central bank's serious commitment to maintaining the accommodative monetary policy stance to support economic growth. For FX and bond markets, this represents continued pressure to keep the overall interest rate environment low, which could maintain downward pressure on VND deposit rates but may also signal ongoing liquidity management challenges in the banking system.

high.title: State Bank of Vietnam: Isolated Phenomenon of Some Banks Raising Interest Rates
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam issued an official press release emphasizing that recent interest rate increases by some banks are "isolated phenomena." The SBV reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining stable market interest rates and keeping policy rates unchanged to provide low-cost funding access for credit institutions. The central bank highlighted its March 30 directive requiring banks to stabilize market interest rates and the April 9 meeting with commercial banks to implement government policy on reducing interest rate levels. This statement reinforces the SBV's dovish stance and suggests continued monetary accommodation. For bond investors, this indicates sustained low policy rates, while VND traders should monitor for any signs of banking system liquidity stress that might necessitate future intervention.

high.title: Foreign Investors Dramatically Sell Net 6,400 Billion VND in Mid-May Week
high.summary: Foreign capital flows showed severe selling pressure with net outflows reaching 6,377 billion VND across the entire market during the mid-May trading week. On HOSE alone, foreign investors net sold 6,281 billion VND, while HNX saw 130 billion VND in net selling. The VN-Index fell 44.47 points (-2.31%) to close at 1,877.13 points, with major large-cap stocks like Vingroup and banking stocks leading the decline. Heavy selling concentrated on banking stocks and blue chips, with ACB experiencing the strongest net selling at around 600 million VND. This represents the most significant foreign selling since mid-April 2026, indicating potential concerns about Vietnamese market valuations or broader emerging market risk-off sentiment. Such capital outflows could create downward pressure on the VND and may influence SBV's FX intervention decisions.

medium.title: Chairman Announces Return to 'Race Track', VNDirect Stock Hits Ceiling
medium.summary: VN-Index dropped nearly 20 points to 1,877 points amid heavy foreign selling of over 3,200 billion VND on HOSE. However, securities stocks surged, with VND hitting the ceiling at 6.7% gain to 17,450 VND/share on explosive volume of over 45.4 million shares, driven by management's "return to race track" announcement.

medium.title: When Will Fed Cut Interest Rates?: Series of Banks Change 180 Degrees, Excluding One Possibility
medium.summary: Major financial institutions including Morgan Stanley and Barclays have ruled out Fed rate cuts this year due to rising oil prices from Middle East conflicts and increased inflation concerns from the Iran conflict. This hawkish shift in Fed expectations could influence SBV policy decisions and VND strength.

medium.title: Gold Bars Drop to Lowest Level in Over 4 Months, What Do Experts Advise?
medium.summary: International gold prices fell to 4,504 USD/ounce while domestic gold prices dropped 400,000 VND/tael to 159-162 million VND/tael for SJC gold bars. The decline reflects stronger USD and rising oil prices increasing inflation concerns, potentially affecting Fed policy expectations and regional monetary policy decisions.

medium.title: Two Important Indicators Help Investors Identify Potential Stocks Amid VN-Index Strong Divergence
medium.summary: MoneyGain's analysis reveals that VIN group stocks (VIC, VHM, VRE, VPL) contributed 245.9 points to VN-Index's recent 270-point gain, representing 91% of the index increase. This extreme market concentration highlights significant divergence in Vietnamese equity performance, relevant for understanding capital flow patterns.
